register.rule: integer cents on a double-entry ledger; every movement is one balanced transaction; balances sum to zero
register.caveat: structural claim only (conservation, atomic transfers); no interest, inflation, taxes or foreign exchange

register.rule: money enters from declared source accounts: endowments at genesis, a fixed household income per day, the rest of the world buying nothing and selling hardware and energy
register.caveat: household income is exogenous and constant; there is no credit creation beyond lenders' own funds, no macro feedback from firms' wages to household demand

register.rule: transfers settle instantly and finally
register.caveat: no clearing delay, float, chargeback or payment failure other than insufficient funds

register.rule: capability grants with scope, 30-day spending limits and expiry; organisations act through roles
register.caveat: limits are applied to one-off payments only (red-team finding money.delegated_spending_limit_bypass)

register.rule: requests per offering-hour ~ Poisson(sum of its customers' rates); rates drawn uniformly per consumer; an optional sinusoidal daily cycle (`diurnal`, `peak_hour`)
register.caveat: rate distribution and cycle shape are parameters; no weekly or seasonal pattern, no bursts

register.rule: each consumer has a willingness to pay (base price x uniform multiplier); utility falls with price relative to it and requests are reduced accordingly
register.caveat: functional form and spread chosen, not estimated; see `price_elasticity` for the value the simulation actually produces

register.rule: consumer spending is paid from one budgeted pool that cannot go negative, so aggregate demand is budget-constrained
register.caveat: one pooled budget for all households: no individual budgets, saving or borrowing

register.rule: consumers shop among at most six offerings they know, by a weighted utility of experienced quality, latency and price with individual preference weights
register.caveat: weights drawn from a fixed distribution per world

register.rule: a consumer learns of an offering through organic search for its need, sponsored results, forum posts and word of mouth from six neighbours on a small-world graph
register.caveat: search and word-of-mouth rates are per-family parameters; consumers do not browse web sites

register.rule: satisfaction is an exponential average of experienced utility; dissatisfied or unserved consumers switch, damped by individual loyalty
register.caveat: see `retention_and_churn` for the simulated retention it produces

register.rule: a constant share of consumers leaves each day and is replaced by newcomers with fresh preferences
register.caveat: constant hazard independent of age, satisfaction or the economy; population size is fixed

register.rule: a few real requests per offering-hour are executed and verified; the rest are extrapolated from them
register.caveat: per-request quality and cost are sampling estimates, not per-request truth

register.rule: customers leave ratings and reviews, and open support tickets when failure rates exceed 5%
register.caveat: thresholds and propensities chosen

register.rule: thousands of consumers are rows of arrays updated by vectorised rules
register.caveat: they do not reason, negotiate or read; they are a demand model, not agents

register.rule: (4.0, off by default) structurally different consumer rule sets and heterogeneous segments selected by configuration
register.caveat: which rule set resembles real customers is exactly the open question; none is fitted

register.rule: (4.0, off by default) latent needs become active as verified volume served in a source need grows (saturating response with a lag)
register.caveat: functional form and lags chosen

register.rule: value comes from a finite set of problem formats with exact verifiers holding ground truth
register.caveat: eight formats; real demand for software is open-ended and rarely exactly verifiable

register.rule: agent code really runs; measured CPU (or executed lines in the deterministic model) times a work scale consumes compute units
register.caveat: the deterministic cost model undercounts native-code work; one machine type

register.rule: an instance has cores x 100,000 compute units per hour; requests beyond that are refused (503)
register.caveat: capacity resets on the hour; no queueing or latency degradation before refusal

register.rule: providers post a price per core-hour that moves by a fixed rule with utilisation
register.caveat: one region, no spot market, no negotiated or reserved pricing

register.rule: each provider draws an outage each day with probability 1 - reliability, lasting 1 to 6 hours
register.caveat: independent across providers and days; no correlated failures or degraded states

register.rule: instances are billed hourly; an unpaid bill suspends the instance and 72 hours later terminates it
anyone may become a provider and buy cores at a fixed price with a fixed delivery lead time
register.caveat: fixed price and lead time; no depreciation, energy price or supply constraint

register.rule: incumbents reprice toward observed competition and capacity, add capacity when overloaded, start R&D when out-rated, hire when queues grow
register.caveat: fixed heuristics with a few drawn parameters; no learning

register.rule: firm minds keep their own books, publish problems, trial capabilities with randomised designs and adopt on their own measured effect
register.caveat: decision rules are fixed heuristics with traits; no learning beyond beliefs

register.rule: new companies register for a fee; simulated entrants appear by rule or by scheduled shock
register.caveat: see `entry_exit` for realised rates; entry rules are not derived from expected profit

register.rule: a company with claims it cannot pay for the grace period is wound up: accounts frozen, cash distributed pro rata, services stopped, contracts ended
register.caveat: no restructuring, no secured creditors, no director liability; obligations not yet due vanish on voluntary dissolution (red-team finding money.debt_extinguished_by_dissolving_the_borrower)

register.rule: a worker accepts an offer when the monthly wage is at least its reservation wage times a risk factor from public signals (company age, breaches, reputation); unpaid workers leave and warn others
register.caveat: the wage is taken at face value whatever its due date (red-team finding reward.fake_members.wage_never_due)

register.rule: developers progress on assigned issues at a random rate that grows with skill and commit code of a tier set by skill; support staff resolve a skill-dependent number of tickets a day
register.caveat: no effort choice, no teams

register.rule: effort under a profit-sharing rule follows e = 0.55 + 2.5 s (clipped)
register.caveat: an assumed formula, not an emergent behaviour; results about sharing rules restate it

register.rule: a lender approves a loan of at most three times the borrower's verified 30-day independent revenue, at or above its rate, for at most 12 months
register.caveat: repayment start dates and existing exposure are ignored and the metric it relies on counts earlier loans (red-team finding money.loan_counts_as_revenue_and_is_never_due)

register.rule: orders are escrowed; delivery is auto-confirmed after 3 days; unresolved disputes are split 50/50 after 7
register.caveat: arbitration ignores evidence; no reputational or legal cost of disputing

register.rule: only buyers may rate, once each; ratings feed search rank and consumer choice
register.caveat: one rating per buyer whatever was spent; a free order counts as a purchase (red-team finding)

register.rule: a poster escrows a reward paid to the first submission clearing a quality bar on hidden inputs
agreements are compositions of payment, membership, grant, share, deliverable and notice clauses; a missed payment or deliverable is a public breach and a claim
register.caveat: enforcement is automatic and free; no courts, delay or partial performance

register.rule: a mind values an offer from its own position (payments weighted by trust, time, shares, delegated authority, effort), accepts above an aspiration that decays over rounds, otherwise counters or rejects
register.caveat: penalties are priced only when the mind itself must deliver and due dates are not discounted (red-team finding money.simulated_firms_sign_adverse_fine_print)

register.rule: public record of completed and breached agreements; private trust is a Beta update per counterparty
register.caveat: identities are free to create, so a record can be shed by founding a new organisation

register.rule: constitutions are enforced at authorisation; simulated members vote from trust in the proposer
register.caveat: votes do not come from modelled payoffs

register.rule: BM25 relevance times a rating signal times a count of linking hosts; ads are shown above organic results
register.caveat: no spam detection; links from the page owner's own hosts count (red-team finding)

register.rule: highest bids first, one ad per advertiser, each impression charged at the bid up to a daily budget
register.caveat: pay-per-impression at one's own bid; no quality score, no second-price rule, no click model

register.rule: posts, votes and follows; mail with a per-family delivery latency and loss probability
register.caveat: people read a bounded number of posts; no spam filtering

register.rule: minds update beliefs by source and act on evidence records whose references the world can verify
register.caveat: update rule and source weights chosen

register.rule: a firm installs a capability under a randomised switchback or washout trial on real days and keeps it if its own measured effect is positive
register.caveat: see `adoption_curves`; trial lengths and thresholds chosen

register.rule: simulated innovators generate controller programs from one grammar, deploy them and iterate on trial evidence
register.caveat: one grammar family; field trials are the only test

register.rule: daily profit and loss by ledger kind and a journal of operating losses (overload, outage, downtime) derived from recorded events
register.caveat: losses are counted by rule, not valued by the firm

register.rule: triggers and flows call tools as their owner on schedules or events
register.caveat: no partial failure modes of real schedulers

register.rule: agent-deployed and generated sites answer requests with status codes, sessions, consent login, per-app storage, rate limits and outages; a crawler builds the index
register.caveat: server-rendered only; no TLS, DNS hierarchy, cross-site cookies or third-party scripts

register.rule: injection pages, a fraudulent capability, spam and false documentation created at genesis
register.caveat: static adversaries that do not adapt to defences

register.rule: preference drift, demand surges, compute shortages, entrants and reliability storms happen on a schedule fixed by the world family
register.caveat: scripted; not caused by anything inside the world

register.rule: firms, prices, cash, wages, skills and consumer attributes are drawn from uniform ranges set per family
register.caveat: uniform ranges, independent draws; real size and wage distributions are heavy-tailed and correlated

register.rule: every tool call costs a fixed number of simulated seconds and an hourly action limit applies
register.caveat: fixed per tool; real effort depends on content. These service modules are record-keeping interfaces (profiles, self-goals, documents, calendars, issues, tickets, repositories) with no behavioural rule of their own

register.rule: yields depend on machine settings on parametric response surfaces; machines wear and break down; energy grids curtail when demand exceeds capacity
register.caveat: response surfaces and wear laws are chosen parametric forms

register.rule: goods move on links with transit time, cost and daily capacity; congestion delays and reprices
households choose products by a linear utility in attributes, price and distance with Gumbel noise, within a budget, after discovering products by search and word of mouth
register.caveat: a standard discrete-choice functional form with chosen coefficients; not estimated

register.rule: a static per-hour flow model on a capacitated network with queueing delay and drops
register.caveat: no packet dynamics, no fixed point after drops

register.caveat: scripted; not caused by anything inside the world

register.rule: firms, prices, cash, wages, skills and consumer attributes are drawn from uniform ranges set per family
register.caveat: uniform ranges, independent draws; real size and wage distributions are heavy-tailed and correlated

register.rule: every tool call costs a fixed number of simulated seconds and an hourly action limit applies
register.caveat: fixed per tool; real effort depends on content. These service modules are record-keeping interfaces (profiles, self-goals, documents, calendars, issues, tickets, repositories) with no behavioural rule of their own

register.rule: yields depend on machine settings on parametric response surfaces; machines wear and break down; energy grids curtail when demand exceeds capacity
register.caveat: response surfaces and wear laws are chosen parametric forms

register.rule: goods move on links with transit time, cost and daily capacity; congestion delays and reprices
households choose products by a linear utility in attributes, price and distance with Gumbel noise, within a budget, after discovering products by search and word of mouth
register.caveat: a standard discrete-choice functional form with chosen coefficients; not estimated

register.rule: a static per-hour flow model on a capacitated network with queueing delay and drops
register.caveat: no packet dynamics, no fixed point after drops

adoption_curves.how_measured: customers per offering at the last hourly market update of each simulated day (consumers.hour events); days counted from the offering's first day in the market
adoption_curves.qualitative_check: diffusion curves are typically S-shaped (growth accelerates, then slows); `share_with_interior_inflection` is the share of offerings whose fastest growth is neither on the first nor on the last day observed. Reported, not used to set any register status

retention_and_churn.how_measured: event log replayed to every day boundary; share of customers of an offering still with the same offering h days later (pooled over offerings and days); consumer turnover counts as leaving

price_elasticity.how_measured: for every in-world price change of an API offering with 2 full days of demand on both sides: (dQ/mean Q)/(dP/mean P) on consumer requests per day; the difference-in-differences version subtracts the log change of the other offerings of the same need
price_elasticity.note: observational: in a market whose customer base is still growing (or shrinking) the before/after figure mixes the price effect with that trend - as it would in field data. `per_customer_elasticity` (requests per customer-day) removes the customer-count trend but also the customers lost to the price; `price_elasticity_counterfactual` gives the causal figure

concentration.how_measured: sum of squared customer shares of the offerings of a need (0..1; 1 = monopoly) at the end of each simulated day

entry_exit.how_measured: entries: offerings joining the consumer market after its first hourly update and company registrations after genesis; exits: closed listings of such offerings and companies ended as bankrupt or dissolved; rates per incumbent at genesis per 30 simulated days

reliability_distribution.how_measured: per host and simulated day: served requests / (served + errors + unavailable + overloaded), from the service day counters; outage hours from scheduled provider outages

compute_utilisation.how_measured: rented cores / provider cores, time-weighted from instance events (current provider capacity); compute units used per complete host-day / (cores x 100,000 x 24) with the instance's current cores; overloaded and unavailable requests from the service day counters

demand_timing.how_measured: consumer requests summed by simulated hour of day over the whole run

size_distribution.how_measured: customers per offering after the last hourly update: Gini coefficient and the largest share
